question: When is it permissible to combine prayers (jama'), and do the Hanafis allow it for travel?
answer:
The final issue, before I get back to the other issue that I needed to — because there's two issues I need to do. And we didn't talk about jama'. We talked about qasr; we did not talk about jama'. Let's talk about jama' quickly.

Jama' means you combine dhuhr and asr, and you combine maghrib and isha. There is no other permutation of jama'. You cannot do jama' with fajr; you cannot do jama' with asr and maghrib. These are the only permutations. Jayyid.

The issue of jama' is not allowed by the Hanafis for travel. The Hanafi 'ulama only allow jama' for the Hajj, in Arafat. That's the only time they allow jama'; for them, jama' is something the pilgrims do in Arafat, not even in Mina. And they have their ways of looking at those hadith, because there's at least 10 hadith that the Prophet ﷺ prayed jama' in traveling, at least 10 in Bukhari and Muslim. It's actually very explicit. Nonetheless, the madhhabs, we respect them.

And so the Hanafis — one of them said this is jama' suri, i.e. you think it's jama', but it's not jama'. For example, if asr comes in at 4 p.m., jama' suri means you pray dhuhr at 3:50, and then 3:55 — even more, depends on how much taqwa you have when you pray dhuhr. So our imam wants to push it even more. I wanted to have husn al-dhann and say, you know what, pray dhuhr long, but he was, no, no, 3:59 you pray. So you pray dhuhr, and right before you say salam, you look at your watch: it is exactly 4 o'clock. Then you stand up and you pray asr. This is how most of the Hanafi scholars interpret it.

The response is: this is more difficult than qasr itself. But anyway, that's their position: according to their paradigm there is no such thing as qasr — sorry, jama' — for the musafir. It doesn't work. By the way, this is classical Hanafism. I have many Hanafi teachers who now actually do jama', and they say the evidences are too strong. So there must be a current of modern Hanafis that have this. But the standard fatwa that is given is that jama' is not something that the musafir is allowed to do.

The other three madhhabs, of course, allow jama' for multiple reasons. The Hanbalis have explicitly allotted three reasons. Number one: for safar, for travel, that you may do jama' for travel.

Number two, they say for a type of sickness or ailment that affects your ability to perform salah on time. For example, the hadith of Hamnah bint Jahsh, who is a lady who would constantly bleed. Constantly. She had istihadah, not hayd. Istihadah — it's a medical issue. So our Prophet ﷺ told her to combine the salah, do wudu once. So for example, the one who has urinary incontinence — constantly urine — or some issue, or high fever and he cannot concentrate. We're talking about an illness that affects you. We're not talking about a little hand cut over there. No, you get the point: something that affects you, your wudu is affected, you have an issue, high fever, something. So it is the majority position that you may do jama' of those salawat.

And of course, if you're doing jama' and you're a musafir, you'll do jama' and qasr. But if you're sick and you're at home, you will do jama' without qasr. So if you have an issue of, let's say — a simple example, may Allah protect us — constant vomiting and diarrhea: you're najis, so you will become tahir quickly, you don't know when the next bout is going to come. You will pray dhuhr and asr combined, but in this case you're not allowed to do two; you must do four. So you can combine. This is the second reason.

And then the third reason that is allowed, which is explicit in the hadith as well, is in the masjids when there is a weather condition. So if it's snow or raining, and the people are praying dhuhr, we will say, you know what, we don't expect you in dangerous conditions to come back; we'll pray asr, because you'll get the reward of the masjid. Okay, so we'll pray asr — and maghrib and isha as well. Pray, and then that's it, you go. Multiple times this happened, that it was raining.

And of course we're talking about a rain that's, in those days, muddy, roof collapsing, this and that. And even in our times, if it's snowing, something happening, we don't want to put people in danger. Anything that's a bit of a — not even life-threatening, but it's common sense. We're not talking about a drizzle, obviously. This is up to the imam to see what is going on. So in these three reasons, jama' is allowed as well.
